response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-20
CLINICAL INDICATION: Known lung nodule under surveillance. Admitted with fever. Portable film. Has the nodule changed?
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. S. Whitfield (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-08-21
TECHNIQUE: Current AP, prior PA. Projection differs from the prior. The current film is also underexposed and appears lordotic. Both films are mildly rotated. Upright versus supine position is not shown on either film. Comparability is limited.

LOOK AT FIRST:
- Priority order from the findings. None of these is flagged time-sensitive.
- F1: Hazy right lower zone opacity (consolidation), indeterminate.
- F4: Right hilar and infrahilar prominence, indeterminate. Only one read is recorded for this finding.
- F2: Elevated, indistinct right hemidiaphragm contour, indeterminate. The two reads disagreed (one indeterminate, one stable).

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Current: the trachea is poorly seen through the underexposed upper mediastinum, with no gross displacement. Hazy, ill-defined opacity in the right lower zone with apparent right basal volume loss reaches the lower right mid zone and obscures the right heart border and medial right hemidiaphragm (F1). It is present on both studies. The apparently greater extent on the current film may be explained by AP projection, underexposure and overlying soft tissue, so it is indeterminate. The left lung shows no focal opacity or new confluent opacity. Coarse linear and reticular markings are present in the left mid and lower zones on both studies (F6, one read recorded, stable). Vascular markings reach the chest wall on both sides. No pneumothorax. Small nodules and fine interstitial change cannot be excluded on the underexposed current film.
- Mediastinum / hila: The aortic knuckle is prominent with an unfolded contour on both studies. The upper mediastinum looks wider on the AP current film, as expected with AP projection (F5). The two reads disagreed (one stable, one indeterminate), so this is indeterminate and no change is called. The right hilum and infrahilar region are prominent and continuous with the right lower zone opacity on both studies (F4, indeterminate, one read recorded). The right hilum cannot be separated from the adjacent opacity. The left hilum is not clearly enlarged.
- Pleura: The lateral right costophrenic sulcus is aerated and pointed, while the medial right base is opaque. Subpulmonic or layering pleural fluid is not excluded. The left costophrenic angle is sharp. No pneumothorax. The right hemidiaphragm is high and indistinct medially on both studies with an aerated lateral sulcus (F2). The reads disagreed, so this is indeterminate and interval change cannot be judged.
- Heart: The cardiac silhouette appears prominent on the PA prior and enlarged on the AP current. AP projection magnifies the heart, and the right heart border is obscured on both films (F3). This is indeterminate, with no size change reported.
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or gross destructive bone lesion. Bone detail is limited by underexposure. Chest wall soft tissue is prominent. No soft tissue gas. No lines, tubes, pacemaker or other internal device identified. External radiopaque markers on the prior are outside the lungs. No free gas is identified beneath the diaphragm, but the upper abdomen is underexposed on the current film.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: None can be called. Size and density change of the right lower zone opacity, heart size, mediastinal width, hilar size and pleural fluid cannot be compared because the prior is PA and the current is an underexposed AP.
- Unchanged: Coarse linear and reticular markings in the left mid and lower zones have a similar distribution on both films (F6, one read recorded). Density is not compared because of the exposure difference. The right lower zone opacity is present in the same location on both films, but its size and density change are not comparable.

RECIST 1.1: Not computed on radiographs.

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Has the right lower zone opacity changed in size or density since the prior? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP and underexposed. Projection and exposure differences can make a basal opacity look larger or denser. | Recommend: CT chest, or repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able.
- Is there a right pleural effusion, including a subpulmonic component, and has it changed? | Reason: The high, indistinct right basal contour with an aerated lateral sulcus could reflect subpulmonic fluid, an elevated hemidiaphragm, or basal volume loss. A frontal film alone cannot separate these, and patient position on the current AP is not shown. | Recommend: Lateral or right lateral decubitus view, ultrasound of the right base, or CT chest.
- Is there a right hilar or infrahilar mass or adenopathy underlying the right basal opacity and volume loss? | Reason: The right hilum merges with the adjacent opacity on both films. Mild rotation and the AP projection make hilar size unreliable. | Recommend: CT chest, with contrast if appropriate.
- Has heart size changed? | Reason: AP projection magnifies the heart, and cardiothoracic ratio is valid on PA films only. The right heart border is also obscured on both studies. | Recommend: Repeat PA film when the patient is able, or echocardiography if clinically relevant.
- Is the right hemidiaphragm truly elevated, or is the contour formed by subpulmonic fluid or a process below the diaphragm? | Reason: The true diaphragm is not separately visible on a frontal film. The lordotic AP beam angle on the current film also alters the apparent dome height. | Recommend: Ultrasound of the right upper quadrant and right base, or CT covering the chest and upper abdomen.
- Are there small nodules or fine interstitial changes in either lung on the current study? | Reason: The current film is underexposed with heavy soft tissue overlap, and the clavicles project over the apices. Small nodules cannot be confirmed or excluded. | Recommend: CT chest, or repeat PA and lateral with adequate exposure.
- Has the heart enlarged since the prior? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP. AP projection magnifies the heart, and the right heart border is obscured on both films. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or CT chest.
- Has the right lower zone opacity grown, shrunk, or stayed the same? | Reason: Projection differs (PA then AP) and the current film is underpenetrated. Size and density change cannot be reported across these differences. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral with good inspiration, or CT chest.
- Is the high right hemidiaphragm contour a truly elevated diaphragm, a subpulmonic effusion, or lower lobe volume loss? | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate these. Patient position on the current AP film is unknown, and fluid layers out when supine. | Recommend: Lateral and right lateral decubitus views, ultrasound of the right base, or CT chest.
- Is the upper mediastinum truly wider on the current study? | Reason: AP projection, possible mild rotation, and underexposure each widen or blur the mediastinal contour. | Recommend: Repeat PA film, or CT chest if there is clinical concern.
- Are there small lung nodules or a hilar abnormality on the current study? | Reason: The current film is underpenetrated and low in contrast, with overlying soft tissue shadows. Small nodules and hilar detail cannot be assessed, and the right hilum is partly obscured by adjacent opacity on both studies. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing. CT chest if a nodule or hilar lesion needs to be excluded.
- Is there a retrocardiac opacity? | Reason: Vertebrae are not visible behind the heart on the current film, and a frontal view alone cannot clear this area. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest.

IMPRESSION:
1. Hazy right lower zone opacity with apparent right basal volume loss, present on both films, obscuring the right heart border and medial right hemidiaphragm (F1). Size and density change are indeterminate because the prior is PA and the current is an underexposed AP. A new process within it cannot be confirmed or excluded.
2. Right hilar and infrahilar prominence continuous with the right lower zone opacity (F4). Indeterminate, with no call on size or change. Only one read is recorded for this finding.
3. High, medially indistinct right hemidiaphragm contour with an aerated lateral sulcus on both films (F2). Indeterminate because the two reads disagreed. Subpulmonic fluid is not excluded.
4. Cardiac silhouette appears prominent to enlarged (F3). Indeterminate across the PA and AP projections, with no size change reported.
5. Prominent aortic knuckle with apparent upper mediastinal widening on the AP current film (F5). Indeterminate because the two reads disagreed. No change is called.
6. Coarse linear and reticular markings in the left mid and lower zones, similar in distribution on both films (F6). No new confluent opacity in the left lung.
7. Indication question: No discrete nodule can be identified and matched on both films, so change in the known nodule cannot be judged from these images. The prior report's nodular opacity and small pleural effusion (neither with a side given) are not confirmed by the images and are not adopted as findings.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest, for the right lower zone opacity, right hilum, pleural question and small nodules. The findings give no interval.
- Repeat PA and lateral chest radiograph with adequate exposure and inspiration when the patient is able. The findings give no interval.
- Lateral or right lateral decubitus view, or ultrasound of the right base, for the possible subpulmonic effusion and diaphragm contour. The findings give no interval.
- Review the source images in PACS with windowing.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
